/-!
# Erdős Problem 245

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/245](https://www.erdosproblems.com/245)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos245

open Filter Set Erdos245

open scoped Pointwise Topology

/--
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set such that $|A\cap \{1, ..., N\}| = o(N)$.
Is it true that
$$
\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{|(A + A)\cap \{1, ..., N\}|}{|A \cap \{1, ..., N\}|} \geq 3?
$$

The answer is yes, proved by Freiman [Fr73].

[Fr73] Fre\u{\i}man, G. A., _Foundations of a structural theory of set addition_. (1973), vii+108.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_245 :
    answer(True) ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), A.Infinite →
      atTop.Tendsto (fun N ↦ (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊N⌋₊ |>.ncard : ℝ) / N) (𝓝 0) →
      3 ≤ atTop.limsup
        fun N : ℝ ↦ ((A + A) ∩ Icc 1 ⌊N⌋₊ |>.ncard : EReal)
          / (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊N⌋₊).ncard := by
  sorry

/--
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set such that $|A\cap \{1, ..., N\}| = o(N)$.
Then
$$
\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{|(A + A)\cap \{1, ..., N\}|}{|A \cap \{1, ..., N\}|} \geq 2.
$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_245.variants.two (A : Set ℕ) (h_inf : A.Infinite)
    (hf : atTop.Tendsto (fun N ↦ (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊N⌋₊ |>.ncard : ℝ) / N) (𝓝 0)) :
    2 ≤ atTop.limsup
      fun N : ℝ ↦ ((A + A) ∩ Icc 1 ⌊N⌋₊ |>.ncard : EReal)
        / (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊N⌋₊).ncard := by
  sorry

end Erdos245

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement uses real cutoffs N with natural floor, rather than integer cutoffs in the counting functions and limits.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Writing a(n)=|A∩[1,n]| and r(n)=|(A+A)∩[1,n]|/a(n), the Lean ratio is r(⌊N⌋₊). The map Nat.floor sends the real atTop filter exactly to the natural atTop filter, so the limsups agree. Also a(⌊N⌋₊)/N→0 iff a(n)/n→0: restriction to natural arguments proves one direction; the reverse follows from a(⌊N⌋₊)/N=(a(⌊N⌋₊)/⌊N⌋₊)(⌊N⌋₊/N) eventually and ⌊N⌋₊/N→1. The full quantified equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using either problem theorem.

reformulations.difference: The weaker bound 2 likewise uses real cutoffs and natural floor instead of an integer-indexed limit.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The same exact floor-map identity preserves the limsup, and the same density-limit equivalence preserves the hypothesis. The scratch proof establishes this equivalence for an arbitrary EReal threshold, covering both 2 and 3.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/245 (exact statement, remarks, and references; read through the Jina text mirror)

H. B. Mann, A refinement of the fundamental theorem on the density of the sum of two sets of integers, Pacific J. Math. 10 (1960), 909–915, especially Theorem 3: https://msp.org/pjm/1960/10-3/pjm-v10-n3-p17-s.pdf (read through the Jina text mirror)
review.notes: Both declarations match the source, including the affirmative answer and solved status. Checked pointwise sumset semantics, finite interval cardinalities, coercions, EReal division and limsup, and empty/zero/small-cutoff cases. Infinite A guarantees an eventually positive denominator. Allowing 0 in A is harmless for the universal claims: removing it preserves the denominator and density while only decreasing the numerator; this equivalence was also proved in Lean. The final scratch file compiles, and the equivalence proofs do not depend on sorryAx. Direct source access encountered Cloudflare challenges, so readable text mirrors were used. Freiman's book could not be accessed through AMS; the exact question and attribution were verified against the Erdős source, and Mann's cited result was read.
